claims.label: Single point of gravity
claims.claim_rank_reason: no rebutting candidate in the legal candidate set; competing arcs (dispersed, two-centres) have no chart support
claims.archetype_basis: explicit chart_field zhi_fu and zhi_shi both name palace 1; day stem present on that palace's heaven plate

candidates.label: the moment's instruments are spread across palaces
two competing centres of gravity

claims.decision_guard: A concentrated reading may not be used to justify concentrating spend on a single surface without a separate reach case.
claims.limitations: Concentration is a structural observation; it does not by itself rank which surface should receive the concentration.

claims.label: Restraint as the operating mode
claims.claim_rank_reason: the reach palace keeps a competing operating mode alive; A003 and A004 both challenge a restraint-only reading
claims.archetype_basis: duty gate office (closing/blocking) plus governing star office (teaching/assistance)

candidates.label: the moment rewards volume and repetition
the moment rewards invisibility

claims.decision_guard: If the deliverable requires a large-volume launch, this claim is the first to be re-tested against the reach claim C003.
claims.limitations: The contrary palace 8 display cluster (E085, E086, E095) is left visible and carries the reach function; the two readings coexist by palace, not by contradiction.

claims.label: Display is the reach engine
claims.claim_rank_reason: A001 (teaching-led reach) and A002 (alliance reach) are live alternatives; the display reading is not the only route
claims.archetype_basis: display gate + widest-reach deity + radiance star co-located with a cooperation-favourable stem pair

candidates.label: paid distribution is the reach engine
co-created distribution is the reach engine

claims.decision_guard: Reach built here is display-reach; it must not be reported as trust or conversion.
claims.limitations: The marker 丙加乙 names cooperation; it does not name a platform or a format.

claims.label: Value accrues through quiet channels
claims.claim_rank_reason: the same palace's stems sit at the cut-off and death stages, so the channel is favourable in kind but depleted in force
claims.archetype_basis: generation gate + hidden-support deity + reliability star in a gate-feeds-house palace under the yin-favouring stem pair

candidates.label: value accrues through public, high-visibility channels
value accrues through private, low-noise channels

claims.decision_guard: Private-channel value is slow; it may not be used to promise a fast conversion ramp.
claims.limitations: The same palace's stems sit at the cut-off and death stages (E077, E078): the channel is favourable in kind but currently depleted in force.

claims.label: Announcement through the alliance channel fails
claims.claim_rank_reason: no candidate can be supported against it; the alliance deity itself remains visible as counterweight
claims.archetype_basis: alliance deity co-located with the message-sinks marker and a locked three-qi in a house that presses its gate

candidates.label: the alliance channel carries announcements well
the alliance channel works only for quiet, two-way contact

claims.decision_guard: Do not use this claim to argue against partnership itself; it constrains the message, not the alliance.
claims.limitations: The marker is polarity-tagged inauspicious in the register; the alliance deity in the same palace is tagged favourable. Both stay visible.

claims.label: Three friction registers
claims.claim_rank_reason: the friction palaces also carry sprouting and maturing stages, which limits rather than rebuts the reading
claims.archetype_basis: enumeration of palace-gate relations and stem pairs across palaces 3, 4 and 6

candidates.label: the field is uniform and any palace can be forced
three palaces are friction registers

claims.decision_guard: Friction markers forbid forcing, not acting; nothing in this claim forbids trying a method once and measuring it.
claims.limitations: The counter-evidence is explicit: the same palaces carry sprouting and maturing stages (E038, E041), so the registers are impeded rather than dead.

claims.label: The centre is held under contest
claims.claim_rank_reason: A004 is a live alternative: the centre's own marker is favourable to the guest and unfavourable to the host, so a challenger posture is not excluded by the chart
claims.archetype_basis: centre palace marker register (doubled conflict stem) and its single lodging edge

candidates.label: the centre is neutral and carries no disposition
the centre carries a contest disposition

claims.decision_guard: The centre's own marker is favourable to the guest and unfavourable to the host; do not read this as a licence for aggressive comparative positioning.
claims.limitations: The centre has no gate and no deity in this chart, so the disposition cannot be stated through a gate office.

claims.label: One closed circulation
claims.claim_rank_reason: graph closure verified by CAP-09 over all nine traces
claims.archetype_basis: graph closure of the identical-stem value traces

candidates.label: the chart contains disconnected islands
every palace is reachable from every other by one route

claims.decision_guard: A connected structure argues for one system, not for one channel; the claim says nothing about which route is fastest.
claims.limitations: The ring is a relation over stem values only; it is not a claim about timing or about the strength of each edge.

claims.label: Two axes are already bridged
claims.claim_rank_reason: only two oppositions exist under the chart's own opposition rule; the claim cannot be extended to the other pairings
claims.archetype_basis: both Luoshu opposition pairs coincide with an identical-stem trace

candidates.label: the opposition axes are open cuts
the opposition axes are bridged by value

claims.decision_guard: A bridged axis is a channel, not a recommendation; it says the two ends can speak, not that they agree.
claims.limitations: Only two of the six Luoshu axis relations exist in this chart's opposition rule; the other pairings are not oppositions at all.

claims.label: Temporal weight sits twice on palace 7
claims.claim_rank_reason: structural only: the chart supplies no civil date or clock time
claims.archetype_basis: month and hour pillars share the branch the chart binds to palace 7

candidates.label: the four pillars spread evenly across palaces
one palace receives two pillar signatures

claims.decision_guard: Branch-to-palace binding is derived from the chart's own stage annotations; it may not be extended into weekdays, hours or campaign dates.
claims.limitations: The chart supplies no civil date or clock time, so the temporal reading is structural only.

claims.label: The opening is real but pressed
claims.claim_rank_reason: the pressed-opening reading is supported by two independent marker classes (house-gate relation and stem pair)
claims.archetype_basis: opening gate in a house that presses it, with maximum-stage stems and a gradual-reveal marker

candidates.label: the opening is unobstructed
the opening exists but is pressed

claims.decision_guard: Do not read maximum stage as permission to launch without preparation; the house in this palace presses its gate.
claims.limitations: The gradual-reveal marker is a general reading; the chart does not state a schedule.

claims.label: Subject stem and subject seat diverge
claims.claim_rank_reason: depends on assumption A-001 (subject binding); retained with an explicit uncertainty marker
claims.archetype_basis: day stem placement on the heaven plate of one palace, day branch bound to another

candidates.label: the subject sits entirely in the keystone palace
the subject sits entirely in the friction house
the subject's stem and seat occupy different palaces

claims.decision_guard: Divergence is a recorded state, not an invitation to pick the flattering half; both halves must appear in any recommendation that cites this claim.
claims.limitations: The stem-and-branch reading follows the standard subject binding declared in the dependency assumptions; that binding is assumption-indexed.

claims.label: Auspicious combination on a depleted substrate
claims.claim_rank_reason: the doubled hidden-plate marker corroborates the combination but does not strengthen the substrate reading
claims.archetype_basis: twelve-stage readings for the two stems that form the keystone combination, plus the same stage in the adjacent bridged palace

candidates.label: the keystone palace is fully provisioned
the combination is favourable but the substrate is depleted

claims.decision_guard: A depleted substrate argues for sequenced effort, not for delaying the start indefinitely.
claims.limitations: The doubled marker (E016, E018) restates the combination on the hidden plate; it is corroboration of the same reading, not a second finding.
